backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace train_y with its rank-transformed version before fitting (scipy.stats.rankdata divided by n, or the equivalent ranks scaled to [0,1]). Fit the same RandomForestRegressor on the ranks and return its predictions unchanged. Since the metric is Spearman correlation, fitting ranks removes the influence of outlying clearance values on the splits.
backlog.title: Rank-transform the training target

backlog.spec: Clearance values are positive and right-skewed. Before fitting, replace train_y with np.log1p(np.clip(train_y, 0, None)) (or np.log10 with a small offset if values are all positive). Fit the existing random forest on the transformed target and return predictions in the transformed space; monotone transforms leave Spearman unchanged for the test ranking but change how the trees split.
backlog.title: Log-transform the target

backlog.spec: Extend featurize to concatenate the full RDKit descriptor set (Descriptors.descList, computed with calc on each Chem.MolFromSmiles result, replacing NaN and inf with 0 and clipping extreme values to the training 1st and 99th percentiles). Lipophilicity, polar surface area, H-bond counts and molecular weight are known drivers of hepatic clearance, so the random forest gets a compact, chemically meaningful feature block alongside the Morgan bits.
backlog.title: Add RDKit 2D physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy from the same Morgan generator, so each of the 2048 bits stores how many times an environment occurs instead of presence/absence. Keep radius 2 and the RandomForest unchanged. Counts carry more information about substructure multiplicity, which matters for size-related clearance trends.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Use rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with an atom invariant generator set to the feature-based invariants (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()), radius 2, 2048 bits. Feature invariants group atoms by pharmacophoric role (donor, acceptor, aromatic, halogen) instead of element identity, which generalizes better across unseen scaffolds, the exact situation this grouped CV tests.
backlog.title: Feature-Morgan (FCFP) fingerprints

backlog.spec: Add the 167-bit MACCS structural key fingerprint (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the feature matrix, concatenated to the Morgan bits. MACCS keys encode broad functional-group presence in a fixed, interpretable vocabulary and often help tree models on small ADME datasets where the Morgan space is sparse.
backlog.title: MACCS keys as features

backlog.spec: Compute RDKit atom-pair fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, 2048 bits, counts) and topological torsion fingerprints (GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator, 1024 bits, counts) for each molecule. Concatenate them with the Morgan features before fitting the random forest. These encode longer-range topology than radius-2 Morgan environments and can capture molecular shape effects on enzymatic turnover.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and topological torsion fingerprints

backlog.spec: Keep the current features and model type, but sweep MAX_FEATURES over {'sqrt', 0.1, 0.3, 0.5} and MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF over {1, 2, 3, 5} using an inner grouped validation on the training fold only (split the training molecules by Murcko scaffold, using the seed for the split). Pick the combination with the highest inner Spearman and refit on the whole training fold. Keeps the harness-visible interface unchanged.
backlog.title: Tune random forest max_features and leaf size

backlog.spec: Swap RandomForestRegressor for sklearn.ensemble.ExtraTreesRegressor with the same n_estimators, max_features and min_samples_leaf settings and random_state=seed. Extra trees use random split thresholds, which smooths the piecewise-constant predictions and often improves ranking performance on small noisy datasets.
backlog.title: Replace random forest with extra trees

backlog.spec: Replace the random forest with lightgbm.LGBMRegressor on the same Morgan bits. Use n_estimators around 400, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 10, subsample 0.8 with subsample_freq 1, colsample_bytree 0.5, reg_lambda 1.0, and random_state=seed, n_jobs=8. Boosting often beats bagged trees on tabular fingerprint data, though it needs the stronger regularization given here.
backlog.title: Gradient boosting with LightGBM

backlog.spec: Train catboost.CatBoostRegressor (depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, 800 iterations, loss RMSE, random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8) on the Morgan bits plus the RDKit descriptor block. CatBoost's ordered boosting and symmetric trees are robust to overfitting on a few hundred to a thousand molecules, which suits this small set.
backlog.title: CatBoost regressor on fingerprints and descriptors

backlog.spec: Compute Morgan bit vectors (radius 2, 2048 bits). Build a Tanimoto (Jaccard) kernel matrix K(a,b)=sum(min)/sum(max) on counts or bits between training molecules and between test and training molecules. Fit sklearn.kernel_ridge.KernelRidge with kernel='precomputed' and alpha around 0.5 (center train_y by its mean and add the mean back to predictions). Similarity-based kernels suit scaffold-split generalization better than trees in many ADME benchmarks.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge with Tanimoto similarity

backlog.spec: Use the same precomputed Tanimoto kernel on Morgan bits as in the kernel ridge idea, but fit sklearn.svm.SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=1.0, epsilon=0.05). Predictions are the decision values on the test-by-train kernel. SVR's epsilon-insensitive loss is robust to the noisy tail of clearance measurements.
backlog.title: Support vector regression with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Compute a Tanimoto kernel matrix on Morgan bit vectors for train and train-by-test pairs. Fit a GP via sklearn.gaussian_process.GaussianProcessRegressor with kernel = ConstantKernel times a precomputed-equivalent Tanimoto (implement by fitting the noise-regularized posterior mean manually: alpha_hat = (K + sigma^2 I)^-1 (y - mean), with sigma^2 chosen from {0.1, 0.3, 1.0} by inner grouped CV on the training fold). Return the posterior mean at test points, which gives calibrated similarity-weighted predictions.
backlog.title: Gaussian process regression with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: For each test molecule, find the k nearest training molecules under Tanimoto similarity on Morgan bits (k around 7). Predict the similarity-weighted mean of their train_y values (weights = similarity to the power 3). Fall back to the global training mean if all similarities are zero. This is a simple, interpretable baseline that is often competitive with forests on scaffold-held-out sets.
backlog.title: k-nearest-neighbour Tanimoto regression

backlog.spec: Compute predictions from the existing random forest on Morgan bits and from a Tanimoto-kernel ridge regressor on the same features. Convert both prediction vectors to ranks within the test set and average them with equal weight, returning the averaged rank score. Blending models with different inductive biases usually improves Spearman more than tuning either alone.
backlog.title: Ensemble of random forest and kernel model

backlog.spec: Train three random forests with different inputs (Morgan bits; RDKit descriptors; MACCS keys) using seeds seed, seed+1, seed+2. Average their predictions on the test molecules (equal weights). Each view captures different chemistry, and averaging decorrelates the errors.
backlog.title: Ensemble of tree models with different feature sets

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a 5-fold grouped (Murcko scaffold) inner split on the training molecules to produce out-of-fold predictions from three base learners: random forest on Morgan bits, LightGBM on descriptors, and Tanimoto kernel ridge. Fit a non-negative linear regression on the stacked OOF predictions to find blend weights, then refit each base learner on all training molecules and combine the test predictions with those weights.
backlog.title: Stacked ensemble with out-of-fold weights

backlog.spec: Train 10 random forests, each on a bootstrap resample of the training molecules drawn with a seed-derived RNG and each with fewer trees (about 60), then average their predictions. The averaged result is a bag of bags with extra variance reduction, which can reduce the sensitivity of the ranking to the particular training fold.
backlog.title: Bagged ensemble over bootstrap resamples

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule and weight each sample in the random forest fit by 1 divided by the count of molecules sharing its scaffold (sample_weight argument of fit, normalized to mean 1). This stops heavily represented scaffold series from dominating the splits, which better matches the test condition of unseen skeletons.
backlog.title: Scaffold-aware sample weighting

backlog.spec: Before fitting, group training molecules that have identical canonical SMILES (after RDKit canonicalization with isomericSmiles=False) and replace their train_y with the group mean. Then fit the existing random forest on the deduplicated set. Duplicate or near-identical entries add noisy repeated samples that distort the forest's leaf values.
backlog.title: Scaffold-based duplicate handling and target averaging

backlog.spec: Clip train_y to the 2nd and 98th percentiles of the training fold before fitting, then fit the existing random forest. Winsorizing removes extreme measurement values that can pull leaf averages and degrade the ranking of the bulk of compounds, while leaving the rank order of test predictions basically intact.
backlog.title: Outlier clipping of the target

backlog.spec: Using LightGBM on Morgan bits plus descriptors, run a small random search (8 configurations) over num_leaves {7,15,31}, learning_rate {0.02,0.05}, n_estimators {200,500}, min_child_samples {5,10,20}, and colsample_bytree {0.3,0.6}. Score each configuration with a 4-fold inner Murcko-grouped split of the training fold using Spearman, keep the best, refit on all training data. Keep the total runtime well under the job limit by using n_jobs=8.
backlog.title: Hyperparameter tuning of LightGBM via inner grouped CV

backlog.spec: Train lightgbm.LGBMRanker with objective 'lambdarank' (or rank_xendcg) on Morgan bits plus descriptors, treating the whole training fold as one query group. Convert train_y to integer relevance labels by binning into 10 quantile levels. Predict scores on the test set. Directly optimizing ranking pairs targets the Spearman metric better than squared error.
backlog.title: Ranking objective with LightGBM lambdarank

backlog.spec: Train a small multilayer perceptron in sklearn (MLPRegressor, hidden layers (256,128), alpha=1e-3, early_stopping=True with validation_fraction 0.15, random_state=seed, max_iter 500) on standardized RDKit descriptors plus Morgan counts. Standardize inputs using training-fold statistics only, and standardize train_y. The MLP gives smooth nonlinear predictions that complement tree models in an ensemble.
backlog.title: Pairwise ranking loss with a neural MLP

backlog.spec: On the training fold only, drop Morgan bits that are set in fewer than 2 or more than 98 percent of molecules, and drop one of each pair of bits with absolute Pearson correlation above 0.95. Then fit the existing random forest on the reduced feature matrix. Removing redundant and near-constant bits reduces noise in the random subsampling of features at each split.
backlog.title: Feature selection by variance and correlation before forest

backlog.spec: Fit a preliminary random forest (100 trees) on the training fold, keep the top 512 features by impurity-based importance, then fit the final random forest (N_TREES trees) on only those features for the test predictions. Selecting informative features within each fold, not globally, avoids leaking test information and cuts noise dimensions.
backlog.title: Feature selection by random forest importance

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, fit the existing random forest with three different internal random states derived from seed (seed, seed+1000, seed+2000) and average their test predictions. This reduces Monte Carlo variance in the ranking, which matters since the noise sd of the job score is already about 0.007.
backlog.title: Multiple seeds averaged for the final prediction

backlog.spec: Split train_y into 5 quantile bins and fit sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier on the bin labels with the existing features and settings. For each test molecule, predict the expected bin index from predict_proba (sum of bin index times probability) and return it as the score. Classification into ordinal bins gives a smoother ranking signal than regression on noisy values.
backlog.title: Quantile-based target discretization for classification forest

backlog.spec: Build two base predictors: a LightGBM regressor on RDKit descriptors only and an extra-trees regressor on Morgan counts. Convert each prediction set to its within-test-set rank, then average the ranks with weights 0.6 and 0.4 and return the blended score. Mixing descriptor-based and fingerprint-based views yields diverse errors that help the rank correlation on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Mixed ensemble of trees and kernel model with rank averaging on descriptors

backlog.spec: Compute RDKit Crippen logP (Descriptors.MolLogP), TPSA and molecular weight for each molecule, cached by SMILES like _DESC_CACHE. Build a third score as the rank-average of MolLogP (sign +1) and TPSA (sign -1) on the test set, since hepatocyte clearance tends to rise with lipophilicity and fall with polarity. Final output = (0.5 * current blend rank + 0.5 * ... ) is replaced by a weighted sum: 0.8 * current blend rank + 0.2 * prior rank. Keep the weight fixed at 0.2; do not tune it on the test folds. No new model is fitted, so runtime is unchanged.
backlog.title: Crippen logP and TPSA as a rank-blended lipophilicity prior

backlog.spec: In the descriptor LightGBM, pass monotone_constraints so that the features MolLogP and TPSA are constrained to increase and decrease respectively, and set the other entries to 0. Look up column indices from the Descriptors.descList names (for example 'MolLogP' and 'TPSA'). Keep all other hyperparameters as they are. The idea is to stop the trees from learning non-monotone noise along the two most physically plausible axes of clearance, which should regularise the model on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Monotone constraints on LightGBM for physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: For each molecule, embed one conformer with rdkit.Chem.AllChem.EmbedMolecule (using ETKDGv3 with randomSeed=seed or a fixed 42, and a fallback to a 2D-only zero vector if embedding fails), then compute the principal moments of inertia ratios (rdMolDescriptors.CalcNPR1, CalcNPR2), CalcPMI1-3, radius of gyration, asphericity, spherocity and CalcNumAmideBonds. Append these to desc_features for the LightGBM model. Cache results by SMILES so each molecule is embedded only once across the 15 fits. Wrap embedding in a try/except and keep runtime below the 10-minute limit by using a single conformer.
backlog.title: 3D conformer shape descriptors from ETKDG embeddings

backlog.spec: Add a third model: a feed-forward neural network from sklearn.neural_network.MLPRegressor with hidden layers (256, 64), ReLU, alpha=1e-2, early_stopping=True with a 10% validation split, and max_iter=500. Its inputs are the descriptor matrix after sklearn.preprocessing.QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal') fitted on the training fold, concatenated with the Morgan count vector scaled by log1p. Average 5 networks trained with seeds seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4. Rank-average its test predictions with the existing two models using equal weights of 1/3 each.
backlog.title: Small MLP on quantile-transformed descriptors and fingerprints

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, first run the current blend on test_smiles to get rank scores in [0,1]. Keep the 50% of test molecules whose two model predictions agree most closely (smallest absolute difference between the LightGBM rank and the ExtraTrees rank). Append those molecules to the training set with pseudo-targets equal to their blended rank score, then refit both models on the augmented set and produce the final blend. Use only the seed argument for randomness. This uses unlabelled test structures, which is allowed because the harness passes test_smiles and no labels; it should help the model adapt to the unseen scaffolds in each fold.
backlog.title: Transductive pseudo-labelling of the test molecules

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles) of each training molecule. Draw 8 bootstrap bags by sampling scaffold groups with replacement (keeping all molecules in each sampled scaffold), so each bag mimics the unseen-scaffold split used by the harness. Fit the LightGBM and ExtraTrees pair on each bag with seed+bag_index, predict test_smiles, and average the rank scores of the bags within each model before the 0.6/0.4 blend. Reduce ExtraTrees to 200 trees per bag to stay within the 10-minute limit.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped bagging of the whole ensemble

backlog.spec: In the descriptor LightGBM, replace the fixed learning_rate=0.03 with a cosine schedule from 0.05 down to 0.005 across the 400 rounds. Implement it with lgb.train (or LGBMRegressor.fit callbacks) using a callback that calls env.model.reset_parameter({'learning_rate': lr_t}) at each iteration, where lr_t = 0.005 + 0.5*(0.05-0.005)*(1+cos(pi*t/400)). Keep all other parameters the same. The goal is to take larger steps early and fine adjustments late, which may reduce overfitting to the training scaffolds without adding trees.
backlog.title: Cosine learning-rate decay over boosting rounds

backlog.spec: Keep the rank-transformed target y = rankdata(train_y)/n. Change the descriptor LightGBM objective from the default L2 to 'huber' with alpha=0.2, which is the scale of the rank target. Keep the ExtraTrees model and the blend unchanged. Huber loss limits the influence of the extreme-rank molecules, which are often assay outliers in the public clearance data, while still fitting the central ordering that Spearman rewards.
backlog.title: Huber objective on the rank-transformed target

backlog.spec: Before fitting, compute the Tanimoto similarity matrix between training molecules from their binary Morgan (radius 2, 2048 bits) fingerprints, using numpy dot products on the bit matrix. For each training molecule, keep its top 5 neighbours by similarity (excluding itself) with similarity above 0.4, and replace its rank target with a weighted mean of its own rank (weight 0.5) and the neighbours' ranks (weights proportional to similarity, total 0.5). If a molecule has no neighbour above 0.4, keep its rank unchanged. Fit both models on the smoothed targets. This is a label-denoising step that uses only training labels and is fully determined by the seed-free inputs.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-neighbour smoothing of training targets

backlog.spec: Switch the descriptor LightGBM to boosting_type='dart' with drop_rate=0.1, skip_drop=0.5, and max_drop=50, keeping n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.05, and the other parameters. DART randomly drops previously built trees during training, which regularises the ensemble much as dropout does in neural networks and can reduce variance on small datasets like this one. Use random_state=seed. Keep the ExtraTrees model and the 0.6/0.4 rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: DART boosting for the descriptor model

backlog.spec: Replace the single Morgan-bit Tanimoto kernel in the GP with a weighted sum of normalized Tanimoto kernels computed on four binary fingerprints: Morgan radius 2 (2048 bits), atom-pair (2048 bits), topological torsion (2048 bits) and MACCS keys (166 bits). Compute each K_i = tanimoto(X_i, X_i) on the training set and the matching train-test block. Choose the noise sigma2 from (0.1, 0.3, 1.0) and kernel weights from a small grid (each weight in {0, 0.5, 1}, not all zero) by the existing GroupKFold-by-scaffold Spearman search on the training data. Keep gp_mean unchanged and use the combined kernel K = sum_i w_i K_i in both the fit and the prediction. Keep the rest of fit_predict, including the descriptor LightGBM rank blend.
backlog.title: Multiple-kernel Tanimoto GP over several fingerprints

backlog.spec: Turn the fingerprint GP into a residual model. Inside fit_predict, first compute out-of-fold LightGBM predictions on the training molecules using GroupKFold(5) with Murcko scaffold groups, so the residuals are honest. Set r = y - oof, where y is the rank-transformed target. Fit the Tanimoto-kernel GP (existing gp_mean and choose_sigma2 applied to r, with the same sigma2 grid) and predict residuals for the test molecules. The fingerprint-side prediction is the full LightGBM test prediction (trained on all training data) plus the GP residual prediction. Rank-blend this combined score with the existing LightGBM rank at weight 0.5 each, and keep seed handling unchanged.
backlog.title: Residual GP on top of descriptor LightGBM

backlog.spec: Add a second fingerprint family for the Tanimoto GP: RDKit Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprints (rdkit.Chem.Pharm2D.Gobbi_Pharm2D.factory with Generate.Gen2DFingerprint), folded to a fixed-length binary vector of about 2048 bits with the same bit-folding method for train and test. Build the training Tanimoto kernel and the test-train block from these bits, and use it in place of the Morgan kernel inside the existing choose_sigma2 and gp_mean. Keep the descriptor LightGBM model and the 0.6/0.4 rank blend. Cache fingerprint computation per SMILES as the descriptor code does, to stay well under the 10-minute job limit.
backlog.title: Gobbi 2D pharmacophore fingerprints as a GP kernel

backlog.spec: Instead of using only the final LightGBM model, train the descriptor LightGBM once with n_estimators=400 and learning_rate=0.03 as now, then predict the test set at several checkpoints with lgbm.predict(X, num_iteration=k) for k in {100, 200, 300, 400}. Average the four predictions after ranking each, and use that averaged rank as the descriptor score in the existing 0.6/0.4 blend. This gives a cheap, smooth stopping-time ensemble with no extra training cost. Keep all other parts of fit_predict unchanged.
backlog.title: Snapshot ensemble over LightGBM boosting rounds

backlog.spec: Add a standardization step applied to every SMILES before any featurization (desc_features, bit_fingerprints, and the scaffold computation in choose_sigma2). Parse each SMILES, keep the largest covalently bonded fragment (sort fragments by heavy-atom count and keep the largest), neutralize formal charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, and re-canonicalize with Chem.MolToSmiles. Fall back to the original SMILES if parsing fails. Use the standardized strings consistently for all train and test features and for the Murcko scaffold groups. Leave the rest of the model unchanged.
backlog.title: Standardize molecules before featurization

backlog.spec: After computing the blended test scores, refine them by label-propagation-style smoothing over the test set. Compute the Tanimoto matrix among test molecules from the Morgan bits. For each test molecule, average its own blended rank score with the scores of its k=5 most similar other test molecules, weighted by Tanimoto similarity, with a mixing weight alpha=0.3 on the neighbour average. Re-rank the final output to [0,1]. Only test-side information is used, so no test labels are involved. Keep the training pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Transductive smoothing of test predictions over the test-test similarity graph

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 0.6/0.4 rank blend with a weight search. Use three rank-normalized components: the descriptor LightGBM prediction, the Tanimoto GP prediction, and an equal-weight average of the two. Inside fit_predict, compute out-of-fold predictions of the two base models on the training data with GroupKFold(5) over Murcko scaffolds, then grid-search blend weights on the simplex with step 0.1 to maximize Spearman against the rank-transformed training target. Apply the chosen weights to the test-set ranks of the full-data models. Keep the seed argument for LightGBM and the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Blend weights chosen by inner grouped CV over three model ranks

backlog.spec: Replace the global Tanimoto GP prediction with a local one. For each test molecule, select the k=150 training molecules with highest Tanimoto similarity to it, then solve the GP mean formula (gp_mean with the chosen sigma2) using only that neighbour set, with the Tanimoto kernel restricted to those molecules. Process test molecules in batches of 64 to bound memory, and use the same sigma2 chosen by choose_sigma2 on the full training set. This gives a locally adaptive kernel model. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Local GP on the k most similar training molecules

backlog.spec: Adjust the descriptor LightGBM toward stronger regularization. Set extra_trees=True, reg_lambda=5.0, min_child_samples=20, colsample_bytree=0.3 and add feature_fraction_bynode=0.5, while keeping n_estimators=600 and learning_rate=0.02. Keep subsample=0.8 and subsample_freq=1 and the rank-transformed target. Everything else in fit_predict stays unchanged, including the GP fingerprint model and the 0.6/0.4 rank blend.
backlog.title: Regularized LightGBM with extra-trees splits and node-level feature sampling

backlog.spec: Add a kernel-approximation model on the descriptors. Clip the descriptor matrix, standardize it with statistics from the training fold, then clip each standardized column to [-5, 5]. Build 1000 random Fourier features for an RBF kernel with bandwidth set to the median pairwise distance of the training set and the seed controlling the random frequencies. Fit ridge regression with alpha=1.0 on the rank-transformed target and predict the test set. Rank-average this prediction with the existing descriptor LightGBM and GP predictions in equal thirds. The seed argument controls the random frequencies.
backlog.title: Random Fourier features on descriptors with ridge regression as a smooth second model

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, remove the GroupKFold search in choose_sigma2. Instead choose the GP noise sigma2 by maximizing the GP log marginal likelihood on the full training kernel K_tr. Use scipy.optimize.minimize_scalar over log(sigma2) in [log 0.02, log 3]. The objective is 0.5*y'alpha + sum(log diag(L)) with L = cholesky(K + sigma2*I) and y centred by its mean. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Type-II maximum-likelihood GP noise

backlog.spec: Replace the Tanimoto kernel in the GP with K_p = K ** p, where p is chosen from {1, 2, 3} jointly with sigma2 by the existing inner grouped CV loop in choose_sigma2, using the same Spearman criterion. Powering a similarity in [0,1] emphasises close neighbours and suppresses weak similarity, which may help on scaffold-disjoint folds. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Sharpened Tanimoto kernel via power

backlog.spec: Build a second kernel from the RDKit descriptor matrix. Standardize desc_features with training-set mean and std, clip to [-5, 5], and compute an RBF kernel exp(-||x-x'||^2 / (2*d)), where d is the number of descriptors. Use the elementwise product K_tanimoto * K_rbf as the GP kernel and choose sigma2 with the existing grouped CV loop. A molecule then counts as similar only when both its substructure fingerprint and its physchem profile agree. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Product kernel of Tanimoto and RBF on descriptors

backlog.spec: Give each training molecule its own noise variance in the GP. For each training molecule compute its local density as the mean Tanimoto similarity to its 5 nearest training neighbours. Set noise_i = sigma2 * (1 + c / (density_i + 0.05)) with c = 0.5, so sparse molecules are regularised more. Solve (K + diag(noise)) alpha = y - mean as before, and keep sigma2 chosen by the existing CV loop. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Density-dependent heteroscedastic GP noise

backlog.spec: Replace the Morgan bit Tanimoto kernel with a Weisfeiler-Lehman subtree kernel on the molecular graph. Start with atom labels from atomic number, degree, formal charge, and aromaticity. Run 3 WL refinement iterations, where each atom's label is a hash of its own label and the sorted labels of its neighbours. Count label occurrences per molecule over all iterations to get a sparse count vector, normalise each vector to unit L2 norm, and use the dot product as the kernel. Keep sigma2 chosen by the existing CV loop and the descriptor LightGBM blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Weisfeiler-Lehman subtree kernel for the GP

backlog.spec: Build an ensemble of 10 GP members. Each member uses a random 50% subset of the 2048 Morgan bits, drawn with a seed-derived RandomState, and computes its own Tanimoto kernel and CV-chosen sigma2. Average the member predictions on the test set before the rank blend with the descriptor LightGBM. Each member sees only part of the substructure space, so the average is less dependent on any single bit family.
backlog.title: Random-subspace GP ensemble over fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Fit the descriptor LightGBM as before. Use its leaf indices (lgbm.predict(X, pred_leaf=True)) as a categorical fingerprint: one-hot encode each (tree, leaf) pair into a sparse binary vector. Define a Tanimoto-style kernel on these vectors using the same formula as tanimoto(), and fit the GP mean on it with sigma2 chosen by the existing CV loop. The resulting kernel measures how often two molecules fall into the same leaves, which is a learned similarity. Blend its rank with the Morgan GP and the LightGBM rank using equal weights.
backlog.title: Tree-leaf embedding kernel

backlog.spec: Replace the single descriptor LightGBM fit with three cosine-restart cycles. Each cycle trains 150 trees, starting with learning_rate 0.05 and decaying to 0.005 within the cycle, and each cycle continues from the previous one with init_model. Take the test prediction at the end of each cycle, rank-average the three snapshots, and use this as the descriptor score in the existing blend. Keep the GP and the blend weight unchanged.
backlog.title: Cyclic-restart LightGBM with rank snapshots

backlog.spec: Append to the descriptor matrix a block of ring-system features. For each molecule, take Murcko scaffold ring systems via MurckoScaffold.GetScaffoldForMol and count ring systems by size, number of rings in each system, and the number of distinct scaffold types seen in training as a frequency-encoded value. Use a fixed-width vector of 12 values, concatenated to desc_features before the LightGBM fit. Keep the GP and the blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Ring-system and scaffold count features

backlog.spec: Before the descriptor LightGBM fit, augment the training set with 2000 synthetic rows. Each synthetic row is a convex combination lambda*x_i + (1-lambda)*x_j of two standardized descriptor rows with lambda ~ Beta(0.4, 0.4) and the same mix of their rank targets. Concatenate these rows with the originals (seed-controlled RandomState) and fit LightGBM as before. Mixup smooths the descriptor surface between molecules and may reduce overfitting to individual scaffolds. Keep the GP and the blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Mixup augmentation on descriptor features

backlog.spec: In desc_features, append a small block of counts computed with RDKit SMARTS patterns (Chem.MolFromSmarts, matched with GetSubstructMatches, counted per molecule, cached alongside the descriptor list). Use about 12 patterns: carboxylic acid, tetrazole, aliphatic primary/secondary/tertiary amine, quaternary N, aromatic N-heterocycle, phenol, O-methyl or N-methyl, benzylic CH2/CH3, ester, amide, sulfonamide, and aromatic halogen. These flags capture ionization state and labile metabolic sites that drive hepatocyte clearance. Keep everything else unchanged, including the rank target, the LightGBM settings and the GP blend.
backlog.title: Ionization and metabolic soft-spot SMARTS counts as descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the target line y = rankdata(train_y)/len(train_y) with normal scores: y = scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rankdata(train_y) - 0.5) / len(train_y)). Ranks are unchanged, so the Spearman ordering of the training labels is preserved, but the spacing of the regression target becomes Gaussian. Both the LightGBM fit and the GP mean are then fit on this target, and the final blend still uses rankdata on the predictions. This is a single-line change.
backlog.title: Gaussian-rank (normal-score) target transform

backlog.spec: Add a third model to fit_predict: a sklearn ElasticNetCV (l1_ratio in [0.2, 0.5, 0.8], 5 inner folds, max_iter 5000) on standardized, quantile-clipped descriptor features (fit the StandardScaler on training data only, clip to the training 1st and 99th percentiles). Its test predictions are rank-normalized and blended with the existing LightGBM and GP ranks using weights 0.4, 0.4, 0.2. Linear models are a different inductive bias from trees and kernels, so they may add diversity cheaply.
backlog.title: Linear ElasticNet on standardized descriptors as a third blend member

backlog.spec: In gp_mean, replace the constant prior mean mu = y.mean() with a local prior: for each test molecule, use the mean target of its k=10 most Tanimoto-similar training molecules (computed from the same K matrices). For the GP fit, the training prior is the leave-self-out kNN mean within the training set. Keep the GP posterior as a residual correction: pred = prior + K_te @ alpha, where alpha solves (K_tr + sigma2 I) alpha = y - prior_tr. Keep sigma2 selection by grouped CV as it is now.
backlog.title: Gaussian process with a kNN-based prior mean

backlog.spec: Cluster the training molecules into k=4 groups with sklearn KMeans (n_init=5, random_state=seed) on a 64-component TruncatedSVD of the Morgan bit matrix. Fit a separate Tanimoto-kernel GP (with the same sigma2 selection) on each cluster. At prediction time, route each test molecule by its nearest cluster centroid and use that cluster's GP. Blend this routed prediction with the global GP at 50/50 before the rank blend with descriptor LightGBM. This adds locality in chemical space that a single global GP cannot capture.
backlog.title: Mixture of local GPs over k-means clusters of the fingerprint space

backlog.spec: Before the final fits, compute leave-one-out predictions of the Tanimoto GP on the training set using the closed-form LOO residual of kernel ridge: r_i = alpha_i / (Ginv)_ii, where Ginv = (K + sigma2 I)^-1 and alpha = Ginv y. Drop the 5% of training molecules with the largest absolute LOO residual (only from the GP and LightGBM fits, not from the sigma2 search). Use the same kept subset for both models. This removes likely label noise from the training data without changing the test set.
backlog.title: Leave-one-out residual pruning of noisy training labels

backlog.spec: Build the fingerprint with a custom atom invariant instead of the default. Use rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with an atomInvariantsGenerator (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganAtomInvariants or a custom list) so that each atom's initial identity includes formal charge, aromaticity, total H count, and ring membership in addition to element and degree. Keep radius 2 and 2048 bits, and keep the Tanimoto GP unchanged. The goal is to make the GP distinguish ionized and ring-embedded atoms, which the default invariant conflates.
backlog.title: Alternative atom invariants for Morgan features

backlog.spec: Replace the single choose_sigma2 pick with a bagged average. Compute the grouped-CV Spearman score for each sigma2 in (0.1, 0.3, 1.0), then convert those scores to softmax weights with temperature 0.02 and form the GP prediction as the weighted average of the three gp_mean posteriors on the test set (the training kernel is reused, so this costs little). This hedges the noise-level choice when the grouped-CV scores are close, which they often are at noise sd 0.007.
backlog.title: Ensemble of GP posteriors over a sigma2 grid instead of one selected value

backlog.spec: Make the GP noise term per-sample. Start with weights w_i = 1 and sigma2_i = sigma2 / w_i. Solve (K + diag(sigma2_i)) alpha = y - mu, compute the residuals r_i = y_i minus the training fitted value, and set w_i = min(1, c / |r_i|) with c = 1.345 times the median absolute residual. Iterate three times. Predictions use the final alpha. This down-weights training molecules whose labels disagree with their Tanimoto neighbours, using a Huber rule, and leaves the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Huber-robust GP via iteratively reweighted noise

backlog.spec: Replace the single fingerprint with a choice among three configurations: radius 1 with 1024 bits, radius 2 with 2048 bits (current), and radius 3 with 4096 bits. Pick the configuration by the same grouped 5-fold Spearman criterion already used for sigma2, jointly over the (configuration, sigma2) pairs, inside fit_predict on training data only. Use the chosen configuration for the test predictions. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the rank blend unchanged. The selection stays within training data, so no test leakage occurs.
backlog.title: Morgan radius and bit-size sweep for the Tanimoto GP

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, compute the z-scored descriptor matrix of the training set and rank training molecules by their mean squared z-score distance from the training centroid. Fit the descriptor LightGBM in three stages with warm starts: stage 1 uses the 40% most typical molecules, stage 2 adds the next 30%, stage 3 adds all molecules. Use lgb.train with init_model (or LGBMRegressor with init_score) so later stages continue from earlier trees, with the same learning rate and seed. Keep the rest of the blend unchanged and predict test molecules with the final model.
backlog.title: Curriculum LightGBM on typical molecules first

backlog.spec: Replace the single GP fit on all training molecules with an ensemble of 20 GP posterior means. Each member draws a random 70% subsample of the training molecules using a RandomState seeded from the seed argument, fits gp_mean with the sigma2 chosen once on the full training set by choose_sigma2, and predicts the test molecules. Average the 20 member predictions as ranks before the final rank blend with the descriptor LightGBM. This is a batch-level resampling of the GP, not a change to its kernel.
backlog.title: Subagged Tanimoto-GP ensemble

backlog.spec: Pick 300 landmark training molecules with k-means++-style farthest-point sampling on the Morgan bit vectors. Build the Tanimoto feature map Phi = tanimoto(X, landmarks), so each molecule becomes a 300-dimensional vector. Fit a ridge regression on Phi to the rank target by scipy.optimize.minimize with method L-BFGS-B, using an L2 penalty chosen from {0.1, 1, 10} by the same grouped 5-fold Spearman score used in choose_sigma2. Use this predictor in place of the GP mean in the final rank blend.
backlog.title: Nystrom-landmark ridge trained by L-BFGS

backlog.spec: After the closed-form GP solve gives alpha, run 200 steps of plain gradient descent on alpha (step size 0.01 scaled by 1/n) to minimise a pairwise logistic surrogate of Spearman loss over random training pairs: sum over pairs of log(1+exp(-(pred_i - pred_j) * sign(y_i - y_j))), with predictions pred = K_tr @ alpha plus the intercept. Use a fixed, seeded set of 5000 pairs. Predict test molecules with the adjusted alpha. Keep sigma2 selection unchanged.
backlog.title: Spearman-surrogate fine-tuning of GP coefficients

backlog.spec: Before fitting the descriptor LightGBM, make three noisy copies of the training descriptor matrix. Each copy adds Gaussian noise with standard deviation 0.05 times each column's standard deviation (computed on the training set, with zero-variance columns left unchanged) using a RandomState seeded from the seed argument. Stack the original and the three copies, repeat the rank targets four times, and fit the same LightGBM settings. Predict test molecules as before. This is input-noise regularization, not mixup.
backlog.title: Descriptor jitter augmentation for LightGBM

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto kernel on the combined set of training and test Morgan bit vectors. Double-centre the kernel matrix, take the top 20 eigenvectors by eigh, and scale each by the square root of its eigenvalue. Append these 20 coordinates to the RDKit descriptor matrix and fit the descriptor LightGBM on the augmented features. Predict test molecules with the same augmented matrix. The eigendecomposition is unsupervised, so it uses no labels.
backlog.title: Kernel-PCA coordinates appended to descriptors

backlog.spec: Extend gp_mean to also return the GP predictive variance for test molecules: var = 1 - diag(K_te @ inv(K_tr + sigma2 I) @ K_te.T), clipped at 0. Compute the GP score as mean minus kappa times sqrt(var), with kappa = 0.5 fixed. Use this score in place of the plain GP mean in the final rank blend. Penalising uncertain molecules moves them toward the training average, which may reduce rank errors on unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Uncertainty-penalised ranking from GP variance

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, before the descriptor LightGBM, drop every descriptor column whose training-set standard deviation is below 1e-8 or whose share of identical values is above 95%. Fit sklearn QuantileTransformer(n_quantiles=200, output_distribution='uniform') on the training descriptors and apply it to train and test. Feed the transformed features to LightGBM with the same settings. The change is to preprocessing only, and the rank blend is unchanged.
backlog.title: Quantile-transformed, near-constant-pruned descriptors

backlog.spec: Before the final descriptor fit, run GroupKFold(5) on the training set with Murcko scaffold groups and train the descriptor LightGBM once per fold with 1000 boosting rounds at learning rate 0.03. Record the mean Spearman of the out-of-fold predictions at each of the rounds 100, 200, 400, 600, 800 and 1000 using predict with num_iteration. Use the best round count for the final fit on all training molecules. The rest of the pipeline is unchanged, and the search is over stopping points only.
backlog.title: Inner-grouped-CV stopping round for the descriptor LightGBM

backlog.spec: Before fitting, regress the rank target on two physchem columns, Crippen MolLogP and TPSA, with an ordinary least-squares fit on the training set, using an intercept. Use the residuals as the new target for the descriptor LightGBM and for the GP (centre the GP targets as before). At prediction time add the linear baseline back to the model predictions for test molecules, then rank-blend as before. This is a target change that lets the models focus on structure beyond logP and TPSA.
backlog.title: Residualised target on a lipophilicity linear baseline

backlog.spec: Append RDKit's ErG fingerprint (rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint, default settings, converted to a float numpy array) to the existing desc_features output for the descriptor LightGBM only. Cache it in a dict keyed by SMILES as desc_features already does, and replace non-finite values with 0. Leave the GP fingerprint, the rank target, the LightGBM hyperparameters and the 0.6/0.4 rank blend unchanged. ErG is a 2D pharmacophore abstraction that is not in the Morgan bits, the descriptor list or the SMARTS counts, so it adds a different view of the molecules to the tree model.
backlog.title: Extended reduced-graph (ErG) pharmacophore fingerprints as LightGBM features

backlog.spec: Replace the descriptor LightGBM with a pairwise model. From the training set, sample about 20,000 random pairs (i, j) with i != j. Build features as the concatenation [x_i - x_j, x_i + x_j] of standardized, clipped descriptors (fit the scaler on train only), and set the target to rank_i - rank_j. Train one LightGBM regressor on these pairs with seed-controlled sampling. At prediction time, for each test molecule t, average over a fixed set of 50 random training anchors a: predicted_rank(t) = mean_a [ rank_a + f([x_t - x_a, x_t + x_a]) ]. Feed this score into the existing rank blend in place of p_desc. This turns the model into a difference learner, which targets ordering directly and suits a Spearman metric.
backlog.title: Pairwise anchor-difference model (learning to rank by differences)

backlog.spec: Add a local linear regression as a new blend member. Standardize the RDKit descriptors using train statistics, clip to [-5, 5], and drop columns with zero variance on train. For each test molecule, compute Gaussian kernel weights over the training molecules from the squared Euclidean distance in this space, with bandwidth set to the median pairwise distance times a factor h chosen from {0.5, 1, 2} by the 5-fold inner grouped CV on Spearman (use the GroupKFold scaffold groups as in choose_sigma2). Fit a weighted ridge regression (alpha=10) on the training molecules with those weights and predict at the test point. Blend its rank with the existing two members using equal weights of 1/3 each. This gives a locally adaptive linear model, which differs from the global tree and GP models.
backlog.title: Locally weighted ridge (LOESS) on standardized descriptors

backlog.spec: In the descriptor LightGBM, change the objective from the default L2 to L1 (objective='l1', equivalent to the median-regression quantile at alpha 0.5). Keep the rank-transformed target, the tree size, learning rate and boosting rounds the same. Use leaf-value refit by L1 as LightGBM does by default. Keep everything else in fit_predict unchanged. The L1 loss is robust to the wide, skewed tails of measured clearance values that survive the rank transform in the mid-range, so it should reduce the pull of the few extreme-noise molecules on the tree leaves.
backlog.title: Median (L1) objective LightGBM on the rank target

backlog.spec: For each molecule, find its most similar training molecule by Tanimoto on the Morgan bit fingerprint (excluding itself when the molecule is in the training set, using leave-one-out during training). Build features for the descriptor LightGBM as [descriptors(x), descriptors(x) - descriptors(nn), y_rank(nn), tanimoto(x, nn)]. Compute descriptors for the nearest neighbour from the existing desc_features cache. During training use nearest neighbours from the training set excluding the molecule itself; at test time use the nearest neighbours from the full training set. This mimics a matched-molecular-pair view, where the descriptor change and the neighbour's label carry information about the property change between related structures. Keep the GP and blend weights unchanged.
backlog.title: Nearest-neighbour delta (matched-pair-style) features

backlog.spec: Before fitting the descriptor LightGBM, fit a ridge regression (alpha=1.0, on the Morgan count fingerprint, standardized) from fingerprints to the standardized RDKit descriptors, using all train plus test molecules as inputs (this is unsupervised with respect to the target y). Replace each molecule's descriptor vector with a 50/50 average of its raw descriptor values and the ridge-predicted values, computed out of sample on the test rows. Feed the averaged, clipped descriptors to the LightGBM. This shrinks noisy or outlier descriptor values toward what the chemical structure predicts, and it uses the test structures transductively without using any labels. Keep the GP and blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Transductive descriptor denoising from fingerprints

backlog.spec: In the descriptor LightGBM, set linear_tree=True and linear_lambda=1.0, keeping n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31 and the other settings unchanged. Piecewise-linear leaves let each tree capture smooth trends in strongly monotone descriptors, such as logP or molecular weight versus clearance, without needing many splits. Because linear leaves use only the features used in the splits on that leaf, keep colsample_bytree=0.5. If the job runs over the time limit, reduce n_estimators to 250. Keep the GP and rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: LightGBM with linear trees (piecewise-linear leaves)

backlog.spec: Replace the GP posterior mean with a graph label-propagation step. Build a symmetric kNN graph (k=10) over all molecules in train and test, with edge weights equal to the Tanimoto similarity on Morgan bits, and zero self-edges. Form the normalized graph Laplacian. Initialize labels F0 with the rank targets for training nodes and 0.5 for test nodes, and clamp the training nodes at each step. Iterate F <- alpha * S F + (1 - alpha) * F0 with alpha=0.9 and 100 iterations, or until convergence, where S is the symmetric normalized adjacency. Use the test node values as a new fingerprint-based member of the rank blend, in place of the GP member, and keep the descriptor LightGBM at weight 0.6. This is a transductive, graph-based smoother that is distinct from the GP's Gaussian kernel mean.
backlog.title: Label propagation over the train-plus-test similarity graph

backlog.spec: Replace the single GP fit on the full training set with a jackknife over scaffold groups. Within fit_predict, compute the Murcko scaffold for each training molecule and group by scaffold. For each group g, fit the GP mean (with the sigma2 chosen by choose_sigma2 on the full training set, reused for all members) on all training molecules except group g, and predict the test set. Average the predictions across all groups. This makes the GP prediction depend on a leave-one-cluster-out average rather than one fit, which damps the influence of any single scaffold family on the test ranking. Keep the descriptor LightGBM and the 0.6/0.4 blend unchanged. If there are more than 60 groups, pick 60 random groups using seed to bound the cost.
backlog.title: Leave-scaffold-out jackknife of the GP

backlog.spec: Replace the single descriptor LightGBM with an ensemble of 6 LightGBM regressors that differ only in their random column subsets. For member m, draw a random mask with 50% of the descriptor columns kept using np.random.default_rng(seed * 100 + m), and train with the same hyperparameters (n_estimators=400, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.5, min_child_samples=10). Each member's random_state is seed + m. At prediction, average the member predictions before ranking. This is a feature-level dropout regularizer on the tree model, so that no single strongly correlated descriptor block dominates every split. Keep the GP member and the 0.6/0.4 blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Dropout-style random feature masking across descriptor LightGBM members

backlog.spec: Replace the descriptor LightGBM regressor with an ordinal ensemble. Compute the training rank target y in (0,1]. Use three cut points at 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75. For each cut, fit an LGBMClassifier (400 trees, lr 0.03, num_leaves 31, colsample 0.5, subsample 0.8, random_state=seed) on the descriptor features with label (y > cut) and the residual target setup unchanged. For test molecules, the score is the sum of the three predicted probabilities of exceeding each cut, which is a monotone-in-rank surrogate. Feed this score (rank-transformed) into the existing 0.6/0.4 rank blend in place of p_desc. Keep the Morgan GP member unchanged.
backlog.title: Ordinal threshold-classifier ensemble on descriptors

backlog.spec: Before the descriptor LightGBM, append to desc_features a set of size-normalised versions of the extensive RDKit descriptors. Divide each count-like descriptor (names containing 'Count', 'Num', 'Mol', 'Surf', 'VSA', 'Volume', 'Chi' not included) by HeavyAtomCount, guarded with max(HeavyAtomCount,1). Concatenate these ratios to the original descriptor matrix, then apply the same non-finite-to-zero and clip step. The cache stays keyed by SMILES. Nothing else changes, so the rest of the pipeline and blending remain identical.
backlog.title: Heavy-atom-normalised descriptor ratios

backlog.spec: Replace the two-feature physchem OLS prior with a ridge prior on a richer set of simple descriptors. Compute Crippen MolLogP, TPSA, molecular weight, HBD (NumHDonors), HBA (NumHAcceptors), aromatic ring count, fraction Csp3 and rotatable bonds for train and test. Standardise them using training statistics. Build features as these eight plus their squares and the pairwise logP*TPSA and logP*MW products. Fit a Ridge(alpha=10) on the rank target y to get base_tr and base_te, as the existing code does with lstsq. Then fit the descriptor LightGBM and the GP on the residual r = y - base_tr exactly as now. Only the prior changes.
backlog.title: Quadratic physchem prior with a wider descriptor set

backlog.spec: Turn the descriptor LightGBM member into a bag of 8 models. For each bag b, draw a random 70% subset of the unique Murcko scaffold groups of the training set, using np.random.default_rng(seed*100+b), so that whole scaffolds are kept or dropped together. Fit an LGBMRegressor (same hyperparameters, random_state=seed+b) on the residual r for that subset only. Average the 8 predictions on the test set, then add base_te and rank as before. This keeps the GP member unchanged and uses the scaffold grouping the harness already uses to stay honest.
backlog.title: Subagged descriptor LightGBM over scaffold-group subsamples

backlog.spec: Add a fixed-weight message-passing featuriser that needs no learning. For each molecule, build the heavy-atom graph from RDKit. Initialise each atom with a one-hot-like invariant vector: element symbol bucket (C, N, O, S, halogen, other), aromatic flag, degree, total H count, formal charge flag, ring membership. Run 3 rounds of h <- tanh(h + mean over neighbours of W_k h), where each W_k is a fixed random Gaussian matrix of size d x d drawn with np.random.default_rng(seed). After each round, sum-pool atom states into a graph vector and concatenate all three round vectors. Standardise and fit a RidgeCV (alphas 1 to 1000 log-spaced) on the residual r. Average this prediction with the descriptor and GP members via the existing rank blend, giving it a weight of 0.2 and renormalising the other weights to 0.8 total.
backlog.title: Numpy GNN-lite with neighbourhood-aggregated atom features and ridge readout

backlog.spec: Add a correction for molecules that share a generic skeleton. For every molecule compute the generic Murcko scaffold (replace all atoms with carbon and all bonds with single, via MurckoScaffold.MakeScaffoldGeneric on the scaffold). Within the training fold, compute for each generic scaffold the mean residual of the fitted combined prediction (use the out-of-fold residual from a 5-fold grouped inner CV on the training set, with the descriptor LightGBM as the inner model). Shrink each group mean by n/(n+5). For test molecules whose generic scaffold appears in training, add the shrunken mean to the final blended rank score in rank units, otherwise add zero. The correction is small by construction, so it cannot dominate the blend.
backlog.title: Generic-scaffold residual shrinkage

backlog.spec: Before the final models, make a soft target. Run a 5-fold grouped (Murcko scaffold) inner CV on the training set with the existing physchem prior plus the Tanimoto GP only, to obtain out-of-fold predictions for each training molecule. Set the soft target as t = 0.5*y + 0.5*oof_rank, where oof_rank is the rank of the out-of-fold prediction divided by n. Then fit the descriptor LightGBM and the GP residual models to t instead of y, leaving the physchem prior fitted on y. Use the seed argument for the inner fold shuffling. This is a one-round distillation that tends to denoise labels without any test-time information.
backlog.title: Soft-label self-distillation of the rank target

backlog.spec: Split the training set into three overlapping heavy-atom-count experts. Compute HeavyAtomCount for train and test. Define expert k to train on molecules whose heavy-atom count lies within the k-th tertile extended by 15% on each side. For each test molecule, average the predictions of the experts whose training range contains its heavy-atom count (typically one or two). Each expert is a descriptor LightGBM fit on the residual r with the same hyperparameters. Blend the expert-averaged prediction with the GP member using the existing 0.6/0.4 rank blend. Use seed + k for each expert's random_state.
backlog.title: Size-tertile mixture of experts

backlog.spec: Train the descriptor LightGBM three times, each on a different transform of the training target: (a) the rank/n target already used, (b) the normal-score target norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n), and (c) the raw train_y rank-transformed inside the fold (the same as (a) but computed from train_y with ties broken by order). Average the three LightGBM predictions after rank-normalising each on the test set, with random_state=seed+k for k=0,1,2. Use this averaged descriptor score in place of p_desc in the existing blend. The GP member is unchanged, and the physchem prior is still fitted on the rank target.
backlog.title: Borda ensemble over three target transforms

backlog.spec: Change the descriptor LightGBM training into a two-stage schedule. Stage 1: fit LGBMRegressor with learning_rate=0.03, n_estimators=400 on the residual r, as now. Stage 2: continue training from the stage-1 booster with learning_rate=0.01 for another 400 rounds, using lgb.train with init_model and keep_training_booster behaviour, so the second stage starts from the stage-1 trees. Use the same colsample, subsample and min_child_samples. Predict on the test features using the final booster. This adds a learning-rate drop at round 400 and leaves all other members, the physchem prior and the blend weights unchanged.
backlog.title: Two-stage warm-started boosting with a learning-rate drop

backlog.spec: Split the 2048 Morgan bits into 8 buckets by bit index (or by bit frequency in the training set). Give each bucket a non-negative weight w_k = exp(theta_k), and build the kernel as K = sum_k w_k * Tanimoto computed on bucket-k bits only, normalised so the diagonal is 1. Choose theta (init zeros) with scipy.optimize.minimize (Nelder-Mead, at most about 60 evaluations) to minimise the mean squared error of the GP's out-of-fold predictions under GroupKFold(5) on the training fold, grouped by Murcko scaffold. Keep sigma2 from the existing grid search at the chosen theta. Use the fitted weights for the final GP prediction on the test molecules. Everything else (descriptor LightGBM, rank blend) stays the same.
backlog.title: Learned bucket weights for the Tanimoto GP kernel

backlog.spec: In the descriptor LightGBM, replace the fixed subsample=0.8 with a schedule that starts at 0.9 and decays linearly to 0.4 over the 400 boosting rounds. Implement it with lgb.train (or the sklearn wrapper with fit callbacks) and a callback that calls env.model.reset_parameter({'bagging_fraction': rate}) each round, with subsample_freq=1 and seed-controlled bagging. Keep the other hyperparameters and the residual target unchanged. The intent is coarse-to-fine boosting, with noisy early trees and more stable late trees.
backlog.title: Linearly decaying row subsample rate in descriptor LightGBM

backlog.spec: Instead of random bootstraps, build 8 training subsets for the descriptor LightGBM, each containing 70% of the training molecules. Pick each subset by farthest-point sampling on the Tanimoto distance matrix of the Morgan bit fingerprints: start from a seed-chosen molecule, then repeatedly add the molecule whose maximum similarity to the already-chosen set is smallest, until 70% are chosen. Fit one LightGBM per subset (different random_state per member) on the residual target and average the member predictions before the rank blend. This favours chemically diverse subsets and covers the chemical space more evenly than random subsampling.
backlog.title: Farthest-point diverse subsets for bagged descriptor LightGBM

backlog.spec: For the Tanimoto-kernel GP, in addition to the posterior mean, compute the full posterior covariance over the test molecules: C = K_tt - K_te (K_tr + sigma2 I)^-1 K_et, with K_tt the test-test Tanimoto matrix. Draw 64 joint samples from N(mean, C + 1e-6 I) with a seed-controlled numpy generator (use an eigendecomposition or Cholesky with jitter). For each sample compute its ranks across the test molecules, and use the average rank as the GP member score in place of the posterior mean rank. This targets the expected Spearman correlation under the model's uncertainty rather than the ranking of the mean alone.
backlog.title: Expected-rank prediction from GP posterior samples

backlog.spec: Add a third blend member. Take the 30 RDKit descriptors with the highest absolute Spearman correlation to the rank target in the training fold, clip them to the 1st-99th percentile, and standardise them. Expand them with sklearn SplineTransformer(n_knots=6, degree=3, extrapolation='linear') and fit a Ridge regression with alpha picked from {1, 10, 100} by inner GroupKFold(5) Spearman on the training fold. Predict the test molecules and rank-average this member with the existing two members, using weights 0.45 for the descriptor LightGBM, 0.35 for the GP, and 0.20 for the spline model. The additive structure gives a smooth, interpretable lipophilicity and size response.
backlog.title: Additive spline (GAM-like) member on top physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Before the descriptor LightGBM, train an unsupervised sklearn MLPRegressor autoencoder on the Morgan bit vectors of the training and test molecules together (transductive, no labels used). Use hidden_layer_sizes=(256, 32, 256) with the 32-unit middle layer as the bottleneck, activation='relu', alpha=1e-4, max_iter=200, early_stopping=True, random_state=seed. Extract the 32 bottleneck activations for each molecule by running the first two layers manually (matmul plus ReLU with the fitted coefs_ and intercepts_). Append these 32 codes to the RDKit descriptor matrix as extra LightGBM features. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Unsupervised autoencoder bottleneck on Morgan bits as LightGBM features

backlog.spec: Replace the descriptor LightGBM's hyperparameters with a strongly additive setting: num_leaves=4, max_depth=2, learning_rate=0.02, n_estimators=1200, subsample=0.7, subsample_freq=1, colsample_bytree=0.4, min_child_samples=20, reg_lambda=2.0, keeping the residual target and seed. Shallow trees limit interactions and act as a regulariser, and the larger round count keeps the total fit capacity similar. This is a single hyperparameter change that tests whether the descriptor model is over-fitting interactions across scaffolds.
backlog.title: Shallow additive LightGBM with depth-2 trees

backlog.spec: Add a linear member fit on the Morgan count fingerprint (count_features, radius 2, 2048 bits) after a log1p transform. Train a linear model y ~ X w + b on the residual target by minimising mean squared error plus lambda ||w||^2 using full-batch Adam (lr 0.01 with cosine decay to 0.0005, 500 steps, implemented directly in numpy). Choose lambda from {0.1, 1, 10} by inner GroupKFold(5) Spearman on the training fold. Rank-average its test predictions with the existing blend at weight 0.2, and scale the other two weights to sum to 0.8. This gives a fast, differently biased linear view of the count features.
backlog.title: Adam-trained ridge-style linear model on Morgan counts

backlog.spec: Before any featurisation, canonicalise every training SMILES with stereochemistry removed (Chem.MolToSmiles of the molecule after Chem.RemoveStereochemistry). Group training rows that share this canonical SMILES, and replace each group's target with the mean of its rank-transformed targets, keeping one row per unique structure. Duplicates that differ only by stereo or salt representation would otherwise appear as near-identical training rows and bias the GP and tree models. Test predictions are unchanged, and the test SMILES are featurised as given. The change is data-side only.
backlog.title: Stereo-stripped canonical duplicate merging with target averaging

backlog.spec: Add a second Tanimoto-kernel GP built on the RDKit topological path fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetRDKitFPGenerator with maxPath=5, fpSize=2048), computed with GetFingerprintAsNumPy. Keep the existing Morgan-bit GP and its sigma2 selection unchanged. Average the two GP posterior means on the rank scale with equal weight to form the fingerprint member, then keep the 0.6/0.4 rank blend with the descriptor LightGBM. Path fingerprints capture linear fragments that the Morgan radius-2 environments miss, which may give a more complementary similarity measure.
backlog.title: RDKit path-based fingerprint GP as a second kernel member

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, train a logistic regression on the 2048 Morgan bits to separate training molecules (label 0) from test molecules (label 1), using 5-fold cross-fitting over the training set so each training molecule gets an out-of-fold probability p. Set the importance weight to w = p / (1 - p) scaled by n_train / n_test, clipped to [0.2, 5] and normalised to mean 1. Pass w as sample_weight to the descriptor LightGBM fit only (keep the rank target and the GP unchanged). Use the seed argument for the logistic model's random_state and for the LightGBM fit.
backlog.title: Density-ratio importance weighting toward test-like molecules

backlog.spec: Pick about 10 simple RDKit targets that are cheap to compute and easy to predict from structure: MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, NumAromaticRings, RingCount, FractionCSP3, HeavyAtomCount, and TPSA. Inside fit_predict, fit a Ridge(alpha=1) on the 2048 Morgan count features to predict each of these from training molecules only, using 5-fold cross-fitting for the training rows and a full-train fit for the test rows. Append the 10 predicted values as extra columns to the descriptor matrix before the descriptor LightGBM fit. Leave the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
backlog.title: Out-of-fold descriptor-stacked auxiliary features

backlog.spec: Replace the least-squares physchem prior (the lstsq fit of the rank target on MolLogP and TPSA) with a RankNet-style prior. Take the 2 physchem features plus MolWt and NumHDonors, standardised using training statistics. Fit a linear score w such that sigmoid(w.(x_i - x_j)) predicts whether rank_i > rank_j, over a random sample of 20000 training pairs with i != j, minimising the logistic loss with L2 penalty 1e-3 via scipy.optimize.minimize (L-BFGS). Use this score as base_tr and base_te in place of A @ beta, and keep the residual and downstream steps as they are. Seed the pair sampling with the seed argument.
backlog.title: Pairwise-logistic physchem prior instead of OLS

backlog.spec: Change the descriptor LightGBM so that each tree sees a scaffold-balanced subsample rather than a uniform 80% row subsample. Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule and group the rows by scaffold. For each of the 400 boosting rounds, draw at random one row from every scaffold group, plus a random 30% of the remaining rows, and build the trees from this set. Implement it by training LightGBM with a custom loop over lgb.train using init_model-free incremental boosting, or, simpler, by fitting 400 single-round boosters with warm start (keep_training_booster) on each round's subset. Use the seed argument for all draws. Keep the rank target and the blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Scaffold-balanced row subsampling per boosting round

backlog.spec: Add a set of 2D graph-theoretic descriptors computed from the heavy-atom topological distance matrix (Chem.GetDistanceMatrix on the non-H graph). For each molecule compute the Wiener index (sum of the upper-triangle distances), the mean and maximum eccentricity, the Balaban J index (rdMolDescriptors or a manual calculation over bonds), the Hosoya Z index approximated by counting matchings of size up to 3, the graph radius and diameter, and the Kier-Hall chi0, chi1 and kappa1 values from rdkit.Chem.GraphDescriptors. Cache them per SMILES as desc_features does. Append these columns to the descriptor matrix for the descriptor LightGBM. Replace any non-finite value with 0.
backlog.title: Graph topological indices as descriptors

backlog.spec: Build a transductive graph over the union of training and test molecules, using Tanimoto similarity on the 2048 Morgan bits. Connect each molecule to its 10 nearest neighbours (excluding itself). For each molecule compute its degree in the symmetrised graph, the mean Tanimoto to its 10 neighbours, and its PageRank score computed by 30 power-iteration steps with damping 0.85, all using numpy only. Append these three columns to the descriptor matrix used by the descriptor LightGBM. Compute the graph once per fit_predict call, and use only features that depend on structure, never on labels.
backlog.title: Test-set similarity-graph centrality features

backlog.spec: Replace the single descriptor LightGBM with a two-stage cascade. Stage 1 fits LightGBM on the descriptor matrix to the rank residual r with learning_rate 0.05 for 200 rounds, and gives in-sample predictions. Stage 2 fits a second LightGBM with learning_rate 0.02 for 300 rounds on the 2048 Morgan count features, with target r minus the stage 1 out-of-fold prediction. The stage 1 out-of-fold predictions come from 5-fold GroupKFold on scaffolds within the training set. The final descriptor prediction is the stage 1 test prediction plus the stage 2 test prediction. Keep the GP fingerprint model and the blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Cascaded residual boosting with a learning-rate schedule

backlog.spec: Before fitting the descriptor LightGBM, identify descriptors whose distribution differs between the training and test molecules. Train a LightGBM classifier to separate training rows (label 0) from test rows (label 1) using the descriptor matrix, with 3-fold cross-fitting to get an out-of-fold AUC. If the AUC is above 0.6, rank the descriptors by their gain importance in this classifier and drop the top 20 percent. Otherwise keep all descriptors. Apply the same column mask to both the training and test descriptor matrices. Use the seed argument for all randomness.
backlog.title: Adversarial-validation descriptor pruning

backlog.spec: Add one domain-motivated feature to the physchem prior and to the descriptor matrix. Compute the well-stirred hepatic extraction proxy E = fu * CL_int / (Q_h + fu * CL_int), where Q_h is a fixed 20 mL/min/kg hepatic blood flow, fu is an estimate of unbound fraction, set as 1/(1 + 10^(logD - 0.5)) with logD approximated by Crippen MolLogP minus 1.0 times the count of basic amines (SMARTS [NX3;!$(N-C=O);!$(N-S(=O)=O)]), and CL_int is a log-linear proxy 10^(0.3 * MolLogP - 0.5 * HBD/HBA ratio). Clip E to [0, 1], take log1p, and append it as a single column to both the physchem design matrix used for the OLS prior and the descriptor matrix. Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Hepatic-extraction-inspired clearance prior feature

backlog.spec: Augment the descriptor LightGBM input with 60 random Gaussian projections. Standardise the descriptor matrix using training means and standard deviations (clip to [-5, 5]) and multiply by a random matrix of shape (n_descriptors, 60) drawn with numpy default_rng(seed), scaled by 1/sqrt(n_descriptors). Append the projections to the descriptor matrix and leave the original columns in place. Use colsample_bytree=0.5 as before, so each tree sees a random mix of raw and projected features. The projection matrix is fixed per seed, and the test features are projected with the same matrix.
backlog.title: Random-projection feature bagging for the descriptor model

backlog.spec: In the GP fingerprint member, replace the binary Tanimoto kernel with the MinMax kernel on the Morgan count vectors (count_features, radius 2, 2048 bits). For count vectors A and B, K[i,j] = sum_k min(A_ik, B_jk) / sum_k max(A_ik, B_jk), computed in blocks with numpy broadcasting over chunks of rows to stay within memory. Keep choose_sigma2, the sigma2 grid, gp_mean and the rank blend unchanged. Only the kernel function and the input matrix change.
backlog.title: MinMax (generalized Tanimoto) kernel on Morgan counts in the GP

backlog.spec: Add a second GP member that uses fragment-based features. For each molecule, call rdkit.Chem.BRICS.BRICSDecompose to get the set of BRICS fragment SMILES, and hash them into a 1024-bit vector (fragment presence bits, using a stable hash such as zlib.crc32 modulo 1024). Fit a Tanimoto-kernel GP on these bits with the same choose_sigma2 procedure, and average its rank with the existing GP rank before the final blend, using equal weight inside the fingerprint half of the blend. Molecules with no BRICS bonds get the all-zero vector, so guard the Tanimoto denominator with the existing 1e-9 floor.
backlog.title: BRICS fragment-fingerprint Tanimoto GP as a second kernel member

backlog.spec: Replace the fingerprint GP kernel with an RBF kernel on a supervised latent representation. Inside fit_predict, fit sklearn PLSRegression (n_components=8, scale=False) on the training Morgan bits X_tr against the residual r, transform train and test bits to latent scores, standardise the scores with training means and stds, and build K = exp(-||z_i - z_j||^2 / (2 l^2)) with l set to the median pairwise distance on the training scores. Keep the GP mean, the sigma2 selection by grouped 5-fold CV and the rank blend as they are. The PLS is fit on the full training fold, so it must use only train_smiles and r, never test molecules.
backlog.title: GP with RBF kernel on a PLS latent space of Morgan bits

backlog.spec: Append two feature blocks to the descriptor matrix used by the LightGBM model: the 79-value EState fingerprint from rdkit.Chem.EState.Fingerprinter.FingerprintMol (fold counts and sums per atom-type class), and the EState index values per atom summarised as sum, max and min over heavy atoms. Cache them per SMILES in a dict like _DESC_CACHE, replace non-finite values with 0, and concatenate after desc_features. Keep the LightGBM hyperparameters and the rank residual target unchanged, so the only change is the feature matrix.
backlog.title: EState fingerprint and atom-type counts as LightGBM features

backlog.spec: Add a small block of electronic descriptors to the LightGBM input. For each molecule, call rdPartialCharges.ComputeGasteigerCharges on the RDKit mol, read the per-atom '_GasteigerCharge' values, and compute the minimum, maximum, sum of absolute values, and the sum of positive charges over heavy atoms, plus the same statistics restricted to N and O atoms. Also count the atoms with absolute charge above 0.3. Cache results per SMILES, map NaN or inf to 0, and append to desc_features output. Nothing else in fit_predict changes.
backlog.title: Gasteiger partial-charge statistics as descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the least-squares OLS prior (lstsq on [1, MolLogP, TPSA] against the rank target y) with a robust fit. Run iteratively reweighted least squares for 20 iterations: start from the OLS solution, compute residuals e, set weights w = 1 / sqrt(1 + (e / c)^2) with c equal to 1.345 times the median absolute deviation of e, and solve the weighted least-squares problem with those weights. Stop early if the coefficients change by less than 1e-6. The residual r = y - base_tr and all downstream models stay unchanged.
backlog.title: Pseudo-Huber IRLS fit of the physchem prior

backlog.spec: Train the descriptor LightGBM with a decaying learning rate instead of a fixed 0.03. Use lgb.train with 1500 rounds, passing a callbacks list containing reset_parameter(learning_rate=...) that decays geometrically from 0.1 at round 0 to 0.005 at the last round. Inside fit_predict, split the training fold with GroupKFold(5) on Murcko scaffold groups, use the inner validation folds to pick the best number of rounds from the checkpoints at 300, 600, 900, 1200 and 1500 (by Spearman on the held-out part of the residual), and then refit on the full training fold with that round count. The seed controls subsampling and colsample.
backlog.title: Learning-rate ramp for the descriptor LightGBM with inner-CV round selection

backlog.spec: Build 8 bagged GP predictions, each leaving out one of 8 Butina clusters of the training fold. Compute the training-fold Tanimoto matrix, cluster with rdkit.ML.Cluster.Butina.ClusterData at distance threshold 0.6, group the clusters into 8 roughly equal-size bags by round-robin over cluster size order, and for bag b fit the GP on all training molecules outside bag b with the sigma2 chosen by choose_sigma2 on that subset. Average the 8 test predictions as the GP output. Keep the physchem prior and blend unchanged. The cluster split uses only train_smiles, so there is no leakage from test molecules.
backlog.title: Butina-cluster-dropout bagging of the Tanimoto GP

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 0.6/0.4 rank blend with a per-molecule gate. For each test molecule compute its maximum Tanimoto similarity s to the training fold (from the Morgan bit matrices already built). Use a logistic gate g = 1 / (1 + exp(-(s - 0.4) / 0.08)) so that molecules close to training data lean on the GP and isolated molecules lean on the descriptor LightGBM. Final score is g times rank(p_fp) plus (1 - g) times rank(p_desc), with the ranks computed over the test set, so the output is still a monotone score. Set the gate centre and width from the fixed values given here, not from the test labels.
backlog.title: Similarity-gated blend between the descriptor model and the GP

backlog.spec: Change the physical-chemistry prior from [MolLogP, TPSA] to a baseline of [heavy atom count, number of aromatic rings, number of rotatable bonds, MolLogP], fitted by OLS on the rank target y with an intercept. Compute these with rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumAromaticRings, Descriptors.NumRotatableBonds and Chem.Lipinski numbers, cache them per SMILES, and keep the residual r = y - base_tr, which the descriptor LightGBM, the GP and the blend then use. Nothing else changes, so only the baseline features differ from the incumbent.
backlog.title: Heavy-atom and aromatic-ring baseline replacing the logP/TPSA prior

backlog.spec: Add a third rank-averaged member that is a naive additive model over Morgan bits. On the training fold, compute the residual r = y - base_tr. For each of the 2048 bits, take the mean residual over training molecules that have the bit, shrunk toward 0 by n_b/(n_b + k) with k = 5. For a test molecule, average the encodings of its set bits, and take the average over bits with at least one training occurrence (0 if none). Add base_te to get the prediction. Weight the blend as 0.5 descriptor LightGBM, 0.3 Tanimoto GP, 0.2 encoder, or pick the weights with a fixed rule, not a search. No sklearn or GP changes are needed.
backlog.title: Bit-level shrunken target encoding as a blend member

backlog.spec: Choose 64 anchor molecules from the training fold by farthest-point sampling on Tanimoto distance over Morgan bits, seeded from the seed argument. For every molecule, compute its Tanimoto similarity to each anchor and append these 64 columns to the RDKit descriptor matrix.
